text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers on Tuesday. Retuers has not verifired these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

* The central intelligence service is needed to stop Namibian civil servants leaking information to the public, a Swapo member of the national council (the house of review) told delegates yesterday during the debate on the controversial draft central intelligence service bill.
* Cleaners at the University of Namibia are appalled at the behaviour of students, who have vandalised the campus in a term-end orgy of destruction.
* The third and last conference on a white paper for a national energy policy started in Windhoek yesterday.

* The ministry of health has contributed N$18 million towards the building of the Dr. A. Bernard May cancer centre in Windhoek. The International Atomic Energy Agency has contributed half a million dollars with a further half a million coming from the U.S government.
* Three of prime minister Hage Geingob's bodyguards are being implicated in a case of intimidation and purposeful destruction of property, which has been brought by a resident of Keetmanshoop.
* Two groups of prisoners have escaped from the Windhoek central prison and the prison at Rundu.
